summary: AstroHealth Mission Control is a real-time Flutter deep-space telemetry application designed to monitor critical astronaut health metrics—such as heart rate, blood oxygen ($\text{SpO}_2$), intraocular pressure (IOP) for Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), and cosmic radiation exposure—for astronaut Dr. Alex Mercer. Built with an aerospace dark theme, the app features an auto-simulation mode that naturally fluctuates vital signs and automatically engages Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) suit suction during high IOP spikes. It also includes a manual override mode equipped with preset condition chips and fine-grained sliders for testing, complete with a live data-link indicator, crew status banner, and modular assessment widgets.
details:
Project Overview

  • Project Name: AstroHealth Mission Control (Deep Space Telemetry System)
  • Context: Developed as a submission for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge, this is a real-time deep-space health telemetry mobile application built using Flutter and Dart.
  • Primary Objective: To monitor and simulate critical astronaut physiological risks during long-duration interplanetary missions (specifically tailored for Mars habitation, e.g., astronaut Dr. Alex Mercer, ID: ASTRO-MARS-04, Mars Hab-1).

Core Health Focus Areas & Metrics

  1. Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS):
    • Tracks Intraocular Pressure (IOP) in \text{mmHg} to monitor fluid shifts caused by microgravity.
    • Categorizes ocular stress into four severity levels: Level 0 (Nominal: \le 21\text{ mmHg}), Level 1 (Elevated: >21\text{ mmHg}), Level 2 (High Risk: >23\text{ mmHg}), and Level 3 (Critical Ocular Stress: >25\text{ mmHg}).
    • Tracks current radiation dosage rates in \text{mSv/h} and accumulates total mission dose over time.
    • Evaluates cumulative absorption against NASA's maximum lifetime exposure thresholds (benchmarked at 600\text{ mSv}).
    • Monitors live Heart Rate (HR) in BPM (normal baseline around 72\text{ BPM}) and Blood Oxygen Saturation (\text{SpO}_2) percentages with visual warning thresholds for anomalies (\text{SpO}_2 < 94\% or heart rate extremes).

Technical Architecture & Functionality

  • Real-Time Data Streaming:
    • Powered by a broadcast StreamController<SpaceVitals> combined with a 1-second periodic timer (Timer.periodic) to continuously stream health updates.
    • Auto Simulation Mode: Applies controlled random fluctuations (_rand.nextDouble()) to vital signs and automates a countermeasure loop—such as automatically engaging Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) suit suction when IOP exceeds 23\text{ mmHg}.
    • Manual Override Mode: Provides an expandable configuration panel with preset condition chips (Nominal, SANS Warning, Critical State) and fine-grained interactive sliders to manually test custom telemetry values.

User Interface (UI) Design

  • Aerospace Dark Theme: Styled using ThemeData.dark() with deep space navy color palettes (#070B12, #0F172A) paired with high-contrast functional accents like electric blue (#38BDF8), emerald green (#34D399), warning amber, and red.
    • Live Data-Link Header: Features a pulsing green indicator showing an active deep-space connection link.
    • Crew Status Banner: Displays astronaut identification and a dynamic health status badge (NOMINAL, WARNING, or CRITICAL).
    • SANS & Ocular Assessment Card: Displays live IOP metrics, severity badges, progress bars, and LBNP countermeasure status alerts.
    • Radiation Exposure Tracker: Visualizes current dosage rates and cumulative mission dose relative to NASA lifetime limits.
    • Metric Tiles: Responsive grid cards displaying live heart rate and \text{SpO}_2 values with visual warning indicators.
